lectures.title: Delete All Method Singly Linked List

cues.en: All right.
In this lecture we are going to look at how can we delete all nodes from the linked list.
So here we have the linked list like this.
Now to be able to delete the all nodes from the linked list we have to update the head and tail.
So in this case head points to the first node.
So that's why this node is referenced by any node.
It's not going to be deleted from memory.
So the first thing that we need to do we have to set the head to null.
So after doing so the first node will be removed.
So after removing the first node the second node is not referenced by any node.
So that's why it's going to be removed.
Then after deleting the this node the third node is not referenced by any node.
It's going to be deleted.
Then when it reaches the last node the last node is referenced by tail.
So that's why it's not going to be deleted.
So we have to update the tail to point to null.
Then the last node also will be deleted from the memory.
Now let's look at how this is going to work in the code.
So we have a linked list like this.
The first step is we are going to create the delete all method inside the linked list class.
So here the first thing that we are going to do inside this method we are going to update head to point
to null and tail will be updated to point to null.
It's going to be like this.
After doing so, all nodes will be deleted from the memory in the linked list.
Then at the end we have to set the length to zero, because in this case we don't have any element in
the linked list.
So that's why the length has to be zero.
I'm just going to go ahead and implement this method also inside the linked list class.
So here after the remove method we are just going to go ahead and put delete all.
So it's not going to take any parameter.
Then the first step is we are just going to update head to point to null and this tail to point to null.
And we are just going to set the length to 0.0.
So length is going to be zero.
Now let's just go ahead and check how this is going to work.
So instead of calling remove method I'm just going to call delete all.
Now let's just clear the console and I will just make it a little bit like this.
Run this.
You will see that after deleting all of them when we call toString it is just printing out something
like this.
Now I'm just going to go ahead and check the new linked list.
So you will see that if I open this it points to the null, tail points to null and the length is zero.
So that's how the delete all method works.
Now the time complexity for this method is going to be all one, because here we are just updating head
and tail and length.
And the space complexity is also O one because in this case an additional memory is not required to
perform this operation.
